content: {"rule": "K-G4", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge uses Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:25 and Luke 1:34 to declare the challenger link broken against C3's claim, which is the kind of verse-based witness the rule governs, though the text never uses the phrase 'cited in' or 'unanswered witness'.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "[L1] Matthew 1:18 \"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost\" and Matthew 1:25 \"knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son\" contradict C3's claim of espousal union", "rule_words": "A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round", "room": "Whether verses the judge itself adduces as contradicting a round's claim count as 'cited in' witnesses under the rule, or whether the rule covers only verses already on a side's cited-in line; I read the judge's use of them as counting them as witnesses, since they are decisive for the verdict.", "why": "The judge treats these verses as breaking the link yet quotes no sentence from any earlier round that pressed them against it and names no round, as the rule requires."}
